title: Finite-field scalar extension of constructible pro-etale complexes
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $k\to k'$ be a unital homomorphism of finite fields. Write $k_Y,k'_Y$ for the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For a sheaf $F$ of $k_Y$-modules set $T(F)=F\otimes_{k_Y}k'_Y$, with the $k'_Y$-action on the right factor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $T$ is exact and takes constructible $k_Y$-module sheaves to constructible $k'_Y$-module sheaves, where constructible means [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. More precisely, if $F$ restricts on a pro-etale cover of a locally closed constructible stratum $Z\subseteq Y$ to the constant sheaf associated to a finite $k$-module $V$, then $T(F)$ restricts on that cover to the constant sheaf associated to $V\otimes_k k'$, with its $k'$-module structure. For every cochain complex $C$ of $k_Y$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], termwise $T$ satisfies $\mathcal H^i(TC)\cong T(\mathcal H^i(C))$ as $k'_Y$-modules for every integer $i$. Consequently, for integers $r\le s$, if $\mathcal H^i(C)$ is constructible for every $i$ and is zero outside $[r,s]$, the same assertions hold for $TC$ with $k'$-coefficients.

source.place: Tag 093V, lemma-tensor-product-locally-constant; finite-field change of coefficient action and exact cohomology comparison are the specialization needed by the residue-layer argument of def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, last paragraph.

proof.text: Regard $k'$ as a $k$-module through the given unital field homomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] it has a basis $(e_a)_{a\in I}$; the basis injects into the finite set $k'$, so $I$ is finite. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] with the constant presheaf of rings $k$, the presheaf underlying $F$ with its constant $k$-action, and the constant presheaf $k'$. After forgetting the $k'_Y$-action it identifies $T(F)$ with the sheafification of $U\mapsto F(U)\otimes_k k'$. On every $U$ the mutually inverse maps are $(f_a)_a\mapsto\sum_a f_a\otimes e_a$ and $f\otimes\sum_a c_ae_a\mapsto(c_af)_a$. They commute with restrictions and with maps of $F$. The presheaf $U\mapsto F(U)^I$ is already a sheaf, since its matching and gluing conditions hold componentwise. Thus, naturally in $F$, the underlying $k_Y$-module of $T(F)$ is $F^I$. This basis is used only for the exactness and finiteness checks, not to define the target coefficient action.

The module-sheaf categories are abelian and sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact]. For a map $u:F\to G$, the kernel of $u^I$ is $(\ker u)^I$ componentwise. Its cokernel is $(\operatorname{coker}u)^I$: the presheaf cokernel is the finite sum of the presheaf cokernels of $u$, and sheafification commutes with this finite sum as an additive left adjoint. Therefore the natural description $T(F)=F^I$ of step 1 shows that $T$ preserves kernels and cokernels after forgetting coefficients. Kernel and cokernel actions are respectively the restricted and quotient $k'_Y$-actions; their underlying sheaves are the same kernels and cokernels after restriction to $k_Y$. Hence the canonical kernel and cokernel comparisons for $T$ are isomorphisms also as $k'_Y$-modules. Tensoring maps is additive on local pure tensors, so $T$ is exact as a functor to $k'_Y$-module sheaves.

Let $i:Z\to Y$ be one of the stated stratum immersions. It gives the geometric inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to $k$ and $k'$: the inverse images of their constant ring sheaves are the corresponding constant ring sheaves on $Z$, carrying each constant scalar to itself. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to obtain $i^*(F\otimes_{k_Y}k'_Y)\cong i^*F\otimes_{k_Z}k'_Z$. The same two cited results apply to localization at a site object $U\to Z$ and give the analogous comparison on its slice. These comparisons respect the right $k'$-action: multiplication by a constant $b\in k'$ on the second factor takes $f\otimes c$ to $f\otimes cb$ on both sides. General coefficient sections are locally constant scalars, so this equality also verifies $k'$-linearity for the full constant ring sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; constant-coefficient identification from sites.tex Tag 00YV

proof.text: On any slice where $F$ is the constant module sheaf of a $k$-module $V$, [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], applied to the two constant presheaves $V,k'$, identifies its scalar extension with the constant sheaf of $V\otimes_k k'$. This holds for arbitrary $V$. Under the comparison $v\otimes c\mapsto v\otimes c$, multiplication on the second factor sends both sides to $v\otimes cb$; thus this is an isomorphism of $k'$-module sheaves. Together with step 3 this proves the asserted formula on exactly the original cover. If $V$ is finite, its elements are a finite generating set, and their tensors with $1$ generate $V\otimes_k k'$ over $k'$: $v\otimes c=c(v\otimes1)$. It is a quotient of the finite set $(k')^{|V|}$ and is finite.

source.place: Tags 0GMW and 093V, lemma-sheafification-tensor and lemma-tensor-product-locally-constant; explicit constant-model calculation

proof.text: Choose the finite stratification for constructible $F$ in [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. On each stratum the local constant models of $F$ become the local constant models of step 4, hence $T(F)$ is locally constant there. To verify finite stalks without requiring any uniform choice of those models, apply the finite-sum description of step 1 on that stratum. By [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] a stalk is a colimit in $k$-modules of the pointed-neighborhood section diagram. Such a colimit commutes with finite direct sums: maps from either object are the same finite family of compatible maps from the section diagrams. Hence the underlying stalk of $T(F)|_Z$ is $(F|_Z)_{\bar z}^{I}$. This is finite because the original stalk and $I$ are finite. Its $k'$-module structure is already the right-factor action, and a finite module as a set is finitely generated (take every element). The same original finite partition therefore witnesses constructibility with $k'$-coefficients. Empty strata or empty site objects contribute nothing and cause no finiteness assumption on an unused local model.

source.place: Tag 093V, lemma-tensor-product-locally-constant, expanded with the intrinsic finite-stalk criterion

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (c) to the exact functor $T$ and the three consecutive terms $C^{i-1}\to C^i\to C^{i+1}$. Its canonical isomorphism is $\mathcal H^i(TC)\cong T(\mathcal H^i(C))$ in the target abelian category of $k'_Y$-modules, natural in $C$. There is no boundedness requirement: only these three terms enter the computation. For every $i$ the right side is constructible when $\mathcal H^i(C)$ is constructible by step 5. Outside $[r,s]$ it is zero, since the tensor product of zero with $k'_Y$ is zero. This gives the claimed unchanged cohomological interval, including $r=s$.
